cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Can You Keep It?
cards.instruction: Use increasingly sensitive details to test whether someone deserves deeper trust.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've withdrawn my college application. Before I authorize you to hear more: what did you tell Mum?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That my sister's plans were hers to explain. May I hear the rest now?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Permission granted. I've leased a bakery. I'll send you the address.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you call instead? Mum uses my tablet and would see it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Change of channel approved. It's her old bakery. You're cleared to stand beside me when I tell her; keep that tablet at home.

reason: Let A explicitly grant access based on demonstrated discretion, then approve B's safer channel before adding the family connection and trusted role.
